title: Ruins of Chiang Saen
artist: Louis Delaporte (sketch, Francis Garnier Mekong expedition)
fit: Overgrown Lanna temple ruins (chedis, Buddha and guardian figures) at Chiang Saen in northern Thailand; the only candidate depicting an actual northern-Thai place. Small (683x450) black-and-white engraving; a rhino appears in the foreground but the subject is clearly the temple-ruins landscape.

title: Wat Visoun (Vat Visounnarat), Luang Prabang
source: Voyage d'exploration en Indo-Chine (Garnier/Delaporte), via Wikimedia Commons
fit: A clean engraving of a tiered-roof Buddhist temple and melon stupa; the same northern-Tai (Lanna/Lan Xang) Buddhist architecture as Chiang Mai's temples. In Laos, not Thailand.

title: That Luang, Vientiane
source: Voyage d'exploration en Indo-Chine (Garnier/Delaporte), via Wikimedia Commons
fit: The gilded, many-spired That Luang stupa amid palms and jungle; northern-Tai religious architecture akin to Chiang Mai's temples. In Laos, not Thailand.

title: River village, from Voyage dans les royaumes de Siam, de Cambodge, de Laos (planche 15)
fit: Stilt-house river village with a covered sampan; a region-accurate mainland SE Asian river scene (generic, not specifically northern Thailand).

title: River with distant mountains, from Voyage dans les royaumes de Siam, de Cambodge, de Laos (planche 25)
fit: Boats on a broad river with distant mountains; a region-accurate river-and-hills valley scene that reads more northern than the current plate (generic Indo-China).
